E1.evidence: Commit ff581a0 ("distance_sensor: minor correction", part of PR #296, merged by the maintainer) shows the concrete defect and its fix in mavros_extras/src/plugins/distance_sensor.cpp: pnh.param("sensor_position/x", y, 0.0); and pnh.param("sensor_position/x", z, 0.0); replaced by the /y and /z names. No issue exists (packet issue_url "N/A").

units_identified: parameter configuration (px4_config.yaml / apm_config.yaml or user launch)
E2.evidence: The plugin looks up a parameter name that the configuration does provide (sensor_position/x) and stores it into its own y and z variables; the provider and the plugin agree on the parameter names sensor_position/x, /y, /z (the config file entries were added in the same PR, a3b59347 "distance_sensor: define sensor position through param config"). With any correctly written configuration the plugin still computes the position (x, x, x): a copy-paste defect in the plugin's own logic, not a disagreement about a name, frame, unit, or value between two units.

E3.evidence: PAIR: parameters set by the configuration are read by the plugin at initialisation.

E4.evidence: Code-level statement only (the fix diff). No observed effect is documented; the defect was introduced and corrected inside PR #296 before it was merged.

notes: Arguable against the rule that a wrong name crossing the boundary is an interface failure: here the name that crosses the boundary (sensor_position/x) is one the configuration provides, and the error lies in which of the plugin's own variables receives the value. The PR #296 discussion also contains a startup failure ("symbol lookup error: ... libmavros_extras.so: undefined symbol: _ZN8mavutils20orientation_matchingEh") between libmavros_extras and libmavros, which the maintainer attributes to a stale or system-installed libmavros; it is a different composition and is not part of the listed fix.
